BEACH RUSH

FIVE DAYS IN 1944

Day one, you arrive at the Assault Training Center in Devon knowing nobody. Day two, a red-haired railroad man from Pennsylvania helps you over a wall. Three days later you hit Omaha Beach together.

W A S DmoveShiftsprint Mouselook and aimLeft clickfire Etalk, act, continue1 2choose what to say CcrouchGthrow grenade RreloadEnterskip a line / yell CHARGE Vthird-person cameraHjeep hornNguide arrows on / off

Follow the yellow waypoint and the radar. In the jeep: W S throttle, A D steer, Space handbrake. On the beach: 1–7 weapons, right click to aim, hug the sea wall, plant the Bangalore with E, then take the bunkers.

ON THE BACK, IN RUTH'S HANDJune, eight weeks old.
She has your ears.
Come home to us, Henry.

— R.

Ruth,

If you're reading this, then the Kid kept his word, and I didn't keep mine. I'm sorry, sweetheart. I wanted to be the one knocking on that door more than I ever wanted anything.

The fella standing on our porch is the best friend I made over here. He didn't have anybody waiting for him. I told him that was wrong, and that he could borrow you and June for as long as he needs. Feed him. Make him the rhubarb pie. Don't let him fix the step, he'll break his neck.

Tell June her daddy whistled her song every night, from Devon to the boat to wherever I ended up. The Kid knows it now. He whistles it terrible. She'll love it.

I love you. I loved you from the first day at the Mishler with your sister elbowing me. You were the best thing that ever happened to a railroad man.

All of me, always,
Henry
